claim: Forskolin is a unique structurally complex labdane-type diterpenoid used in the treatment of glaucoma and heart failure based on its activity as a cyclic AMP booster.
source: Forskolin is a unique structurally complex labdane-type diterpenoid used in the treatment of glaucoma and heart failure based on its activity as a cyclic AMP booster.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about forskolin's therapeutic applications and mechanism of action.

claim: Commercial production of forskolin relies exclusively on extraction from its only known natural source, the plant Coleus forskohlii.
source: Commercial production of forskolin relies exclusively on extraction from its only known natural source, the plant Coleus forskohlii, in which forskolin accumulates in the root cork.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about current forskolin production methods.

claim: Forskolin accumulates in the root cork of Coleus forskohlii.
source: Commercial production of forskolin relies exclusively on extraction from its only known natural source, the plant Coleus forskohlii, in which forskolin accumulates in the root cork.
evidence: This claim is supported by previous research cited in the manuscript (Pateraki et al., 2014).

claim: Five cytochrome P450s and two acetyltransferases catalyze a cascade of reactions converting 13R-manoyl oxide into forskolin and additional labdane-type diterpenoids.
source: Here, we report the discovery of five cytochrome P450s and two acetyltransferases which catalyze a cascade of reactions converting the forskolin precursor 13R-manoyl oxide into forskolin and a diverse array of additional labdane-type diterpenoids.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing enzyme activities.

claim: A minimal set of three P450s in combination with a single acetyl transferase catalyzes the conversion of 13R-manoyl oxide into forskolin in Nicotiana benthamiana.
source: A minimal set of three P450s in combination with a single acetyl transferase was identified that catalyzes the conversion of 13R-manoyl oxide into forskolin as demonstrated by transient expression in Nicotiana benthamiana.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from transient expression studies shown in the manuscript.

claim: The entire pathway for forskolin production from glucose encompassing expression of nine genes was stably integrated into Saccharomyces cerevisiae and afforded forskolin titers of 40 mg/L.
source: The entire pathway for forskolin production from glucose encompassing expression of nine genes was stably integrated into Saccharomyces cerevisiae and afforded forskolin titers of 40 mg/L.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from yeast fermentation experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Plants synthesize an impressive diversity of specialized metabolites enabling them to communicate and adapt to environmental challenges.
source: Plants synthesize an impressive diversity of specialized metabolites enabling them to communicate and adapt to environmental challenges (Mithöfer and Boland, 2012; Woldemariam et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Specialized plant metabolites and direct derivatives thereof constitute more than a third of approved pharmaceuticals.
source: Specialized plant metabolites and direct derivatives thereof still constitute more than a third of approved pharmaceuticals (Cragg and Newman, 2013; David et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Terpenoids are the largest class of plant specialized metabolites with over 50,000 known structures.
source: With over 50,000 known structures according to the 'Dictionary of natural products' (http://dnp.chemnetbase.com/), terpenoids are the largest class of plant specialized metabolites and constitute a vast repository of bio-active natural products including many structurally complex compounds (Pateraki et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to a database and citation.

claim: Paclitaxel (taxol) is a widely used plant-derived terpenoid pharmaceutical with anticancer properties.
source: Examples of widely used plant-derived terpenoid pharmaceuticals are the anticancer drug paclitaxel (taxol) (Liu and Khosla, 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Ingenol mebutate (picato) is used for treatment of actinic keratosis.
source: the therapeutic ingenol mebutate (picato) that is used for treatment of actinic keratosis (King et al., 2016; Luo et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Artemisinin is the most efficient treatment against malaria caused by Plasmodium parasites.
source: artemisinin which is the most efficient treatment against malaria caused by Plasmodium parasites (Graham et al., 2010; Paddon and Keasling, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Traditional chemical synthesis of plant-derived diterpenoid pharmaceuticals remains economically challenging.
source: Traditional chemical synthesis of plant-derived diterpenoid pharmaceuticals remains economically challenging, despite recent examples of elegant strategies mimicking natural routes (Appendino, 2014; Kawamura et al., 2016; Yuan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research and general knowledge in the field.

claim: Engineered total biosynthesis of terpenoid therapeutics including paclitaxel and ingenol esters has not yet been achieved.
source: In contrast to recent examples demonstrating complete pathway reconstruction and production of opiate alkaloids in yeast (Galanie et al., 2015; Nakagawa et al., 2016), engineered total biosynthesis of terpenoid therapeutics—including paclitaxel and ingenol esters—has not yet been achieved.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the state of the field at the time of publication and citations.

claim: Forskolin is the active hypotensive principle accumulating in the root cork of Coleus forskohlii.
source: The diterpenoid forskolin is the active hypotensive principle accumulating in the root cork of Coleus forskohlii (Pateraki et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Coleus forskohlii is a perennial shrub of the Lamiaceae family, indigenous to India and Southeast Asia.
source: a perennial shrub of the Lamiaceae family, indigenous to India and Southeast Asia with numerous reported applications in traditional medicine (Alasbahi and Melzig, 2010b; Kavitha et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The pharmaceutical properties of forskolin are based on its ability to directly activate the adenylate cyclase enzyme resulting in elevated levels of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP).
source: The pharmaceutical properties of forskolin are based on its ability to directly activate the adenylate cyclase enzyme resulting in elevated levels of the second messenger cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) (Doseyici et al., 2014; Seamon et al., 1981).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Approved applications of forskolin include alleviation of glaucoma.
source: Approved applications of forskolin range from alleviation of glaucoma (OcuforsEye drop solutions, Sabinsa, India)
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to a commercial product and citations.

claim: Approved applications of forskolin include treatment of hypertension and heart failure.
source: treatment of hypertension and heart failure (Colforsin daropate hydrochloride, a water-soluble derivative of forskolin, Nippon Kayaku, Japan)
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to a commercial product.

claim: Forskolin has applications in lipolysis and body weight control.
source: to lipolysis and body weight control (Godard et al., 2005; Kikura et al., 2004; Toya et al., 1998; Wagh et al., 2012; Yoneyama et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Forskolin-induced pigmentation of the skin increases protection against UV-associated carcinogenesis in animal tests.
source: Therapeutic opportunities were also suggested in animal tests, where forskolin-induced pigmentation of the skin, increasing protection against UV-associated carcinogenesis (D'Orazio et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Forskolin has a complex chemical structure with a decalin core, a tetrahydropyran ring, five oxidized positions and eight chiral centers.
source: The complex chemical structure of forskolin with a decalin core, characteristic of labdane-type diterpenoids, a tetrahydropyran ring, five oxidized positions and eight chiral centers (Figure 1A) represents a challenge for classical organic chemical synthesis
evidence: This claim is supported by the chemical structure shown in Figure 1A.

claim: A key intermediate for stereoselective total synthesis of forskolin has been reported.
source: although a key intermediate for stereoselective total synthesis has been reported (Ye et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Commercially available forskolin is extracted from C. forskohlii roots and purified from a mixture of over 60 structurally related diterpenoids.
source: Hence, commercially available forskolin is extracted from C. forskohlii roots and purified from a mixture of over 60 structurally related abietane and epoxylabdane diterpenoids with a forskolin content varying from 0.013% to 0.728% of root dry weight (Alasbahi and Melzig, 2010a; Asada et al., 2012; Srivastava et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Forskolin content in C. forskohlii roots varies from 0.013% to 0.728% of root dry weight.
source: with a forskolin content varying from 0.013% to 0.728% of root dry weight (Alasbahi and Melzig, 2010a; Asada et al., 2012; Srivastava et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Reliable and sustainable commercial production of forskolin from C. forskohlii will become unachievable due to low yields, disease susceptibility, changing climatic conditions and resource intensive extraction procedures.
source: As the demand for forskolin grows, reliable and sustainable commercial production from C. forskholii will become unachievable due to low yields, susceptibility of this species to diseases, changing climatic conditions and the resource intensive extraction and purification procedure required to obtain pharmaceutical grade forskolin (Mora-Pale et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and inference about future production challenges.

claim: A pair of diterpene synthases (CfTPS2 and CfTPS3) exclusively present in the root cork catalyze cyclization of geranylgeranyl diphosphate (GGPP) into 13R-manoyl oxide.
source: A pair of diterpene synthases (CfTPS2 and CfTPS3), exclusively present in the root cork, was found to catalyze cyclization of the C20 diterpenoid precursor geranylgeranyl diphosphate (GGPP) into 13R-manoyl oxide, the diterpene scaffold of forskolin (Pateraki et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Biosynthesis of 13R-manoyl oxide in enantiomerically pure form but in low yields was achieved by expressing CfTPS2 and CfTPS3 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, E. coli and Synechocystis sp.
source: As a proof of concept, biosynthesis of 13R-manoyl oxide in enantiomerically pure form but in low yields was achieved by expressing CfTPS2 and CfTPS3 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, E. coli and Synechocystis sp. (Andersen-Ranberg et al., 2016; Englund et al., 2015; Nielsen et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The conversion of 13R-manoyl oxide to forskolin requires six regio- and stereospecific monooxygenations and a single regiospecific acetylation.
source: The conversion of 13R-manoyl oxide to forskolin requires six regio- and stereospecific monooxygenations and a single regiospecific acetylation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the chemical structures shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The root cork transcriptome of C. forskohlii contained 263,652 assembled putative cDNAs.
source: The generated transcriptome contained 263,652 assembled putative cDNAs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNA-Seq analysis.

claim: Members of the CYP76AH subfamily catalyze monooxygenation of abietane-type diterpenoids like miltiradiene and dehydroabietadiene in Lamiaceae species.
source: Members of the CYP76AH subfamily, part of the CYP71 clan, have recently been shown to catalyze monooxygenation of abietane-type diterpenoids like miltiradiene and dehydroabietadiene in Lamiaceae species, closely related to C. forskohlii (Božić et al., 2015; Ignea et al., 2016a; Zi and Peters, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Seven members of the CYP76AH subfamily were identified in the C. forskohlii root cork transcriptome, making it the highest represented CYP subfamily.
source: Among these CYPs, seven members were assigned to the CYP76AH subfamily by the 'P450 Nomenclature committee' (Nelson, 2009), rendering this CYP subfamily the highest represented in the transcriptome (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from transcriptome analysis.

claim: Members of the CYP76AH family were highly or exclusively expressed in the root cork cells of C. forskohlii.
source: Similarly to the previously identified diTPSs, CfTPS2 and CfTPS3 (Pateraki et al., 2014), gene expression studies showed that the identified members of the CYP76AH family were highly or exclusively expressed in the root cork cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Six CYPs efficiently converted 13R-manoyl oxide into oxygenated derivatives when expressed in N. benthamiana.
source: Of the CYPs tested, six efficiently converted 13R-manoyl oxide into oxygenated derivatives (Figures 2A and 3 and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in the figures.

claim: CfCYP76AH15, CfCYP76AH8 and CfCYP76AH17 catalyzed formation of 11-oxo-13R-manoyl oxide as the main product.
source: CfCYP76AH15, CfCYP76AH8 and CfCYP76AH17 catalyzed formation of 11-oxo-13R-manoyl oxide (2) as the main product (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in the figures.

claim: Forskolin harbors a keto-group at the C-11 position, like the majority of 13R-manoyl oxide-derived diterpenoids found in C. forskohlii.
source: Forskolin harbors a keto-group at the C-11 position, like the majority of 13R-manoyl oxide-derived diterpenoids found in C. forskohlii (Asada et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: CfCYP76AH15 showed the highest efficiency and specificity for the conversion of 13R-manoyl oxide to 11-oxo-13R-manoyl oxide with no concomitant formation of multi-oxygenated products.
source: Of the three CfCYP76AHs tested in this experiment, CfCYP76AH15 showed the highest efficiency and specificity for the conversion of 13R-manoyl oxide to 2 with no concomitant formation of multi-oxygenated products (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Compound 5d produced by CfCYP76AH8 and CfCYP76AH17 was identified as 1,11-dihydroxy-13R-manoyl oxide.
source: Compound 5d produced by CfCYP76AH8 as well as by CfCYP76AH17 was identified as 1,11-dihydroxy-13R-manoyl oxide (Figures 2B and 4 and Tables 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data shown in the figures and tables.

claim: The oxygenation pattern of 1,11-dihydroxy-13R-manoyl oxide is found in forskolin.
source: Noticable, this specific oxygenation pattern is found in forskolin.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from comparing chemical structures.

claim: CfCYP76AH16 yielded predominantly 9-hydroxy-13R-manoyl oxide (coleorol).
source: CfCYP76AH16 yielded predominantly 3a which was identified by NMR as 9-hydroxy-13R-manoyl oxide (or coleorol)
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data.

claim: CfCYP76AH11 produced a range of monooxygenated derivatives including traces of 9-deoxydeacetylforskolin.
source: CfCYP76AH11 produced a range of monooxygenated derivatives including traces of 10b which was identified by NMR as 9-deoxydeacetylforskolin (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data and figure.

claim: The combination of CfCYP76AH15 and CfCYP76AH11 afforded production of 6,7-dihydroxy-11-keto-manoyl oxide.
source: The combination of CfCYP76AH15 and CfCYP76AH11 afforded production of 6,7-dihydroxy-11-keto-manoyl oxide (7h) as part of a complex mixture.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from co-expression studies.

claim: The triplet combination CfCYP76AH15, CfCYP76AH11 and CfCYP76AH16 led to the highest amounts of deacetylforskolin.
source: The triplet combination CfCYP76AH15, CfCYP76AH11 and CfCYP76AH16 led to the highest amounts of 13b.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from co-expression studies.

claim: The combination of CfCYP76AH15, CfCYP76AH11 and CfCYP76AH16 constitutes the optimal biosynthetic pathway for specific formation of deacetylforskolin from 13R-manoyl oxide.
source: Thus, this combination of multifunctional P450s appeared to constitute the optimal biosynthetic pathway for specific formation of 13b from 1 (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The root cork of C. forskohlii contains numerous abietane diterpenoids derived from miltiradiene.
source: In addition to 13R-manoyl oxide-derived diterpenoids, the root cork of C. forskohlii contains numerous abietane diterpenoids derived from miltiradiene (Alasbahi and Melzig, 2010a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: A pair of diterpene synthases (CfTPS1 and CfTPS3) mainly expressed in the root cork of C. forskohlii produce miltiradiene.
source: Recently a pair of diterpene synthases (CfTPS1 and CfTPS3) mainly expressed in the root cork of C. forskohlii was demonstrated to produce miltiradiene (Pateraki et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: CYP76AH1 from Salvia miltiorrhiza catalyzes synthesis of ferruginol from miltiradiene or dehydroabietadiene.
source: CYP76AH1 from Salvia miltiorrhiza (Guo et al., 2013), CYP76AH4 as well as RoFS1 and RoFS2 from Rosmarinus officinalis (Božić et al., 2015; Zi and Peters, 2013) and CYP76AH24 from S. pomifera catalyze synthesis of ferruginol, the precursor of carnosic acid and tanshinones (Guo et al., 2013; Ignea et al., 2016a), from miltiradiene or dehydroabietadiene.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: CYP76AH3 from S. miltiorrhiza accepts ferruginol as a substrate to produce sugiol, 11-hydroxy-ferruginol and 11-hydroxy-sugiol.
source: Additionally, CYP76AH3 from S. miltiorrhiza has been shown to accept ferruginol as a substrate to produce sugiol, 11-hydroxy-ferruginol and 11-hydroxy-sugiol (Guo et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Miltiradiene-accepting CYP76AHs show high-sequence homology ranging from 60% to 85% at the amino acid level with those identified in C. forskohlii.
source: These miltiradiene-accepting CYP76AHs show high-sequence homology, ranging from 60% to 85% at the amino acid level, with those identified in C. forskohlii.
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis data.

claim: CfCYP76AH15 converts miltiradiene to ferruginol.
source: CfCYP76AH15 was shown to convert miltiradiene to ferruginol (Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Ferruginol was identified in extracts of C. forskohlii root cork.
source: Ferruginol was identified in extracts of C. forskohlii root cork (Figure 6)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: CfCYP76AH15 is possibly involved in the biosynthesis of ferruginol in planta.
source: so it is possible that CfCYP76AH15 is also involved in the biosynthesis of ferruginol in planta.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the enzyme activity and presence of ferruginol in the plant.

claim: RoCYP76AH4 efficiently converts 13R-manoyl oxide to 11-oxo-13R-manoyl oxide.
source: Transient expression of RoCYP76AH4 (Zi and Peters, 2013), RoFS1 and SfFS (Božić et al., 2015) in N. benthamiana leaves able to synthesize 13R-manoyl oxide demonstrated that RoCYP76AH4 was able to efficiently convert 13R-manoyl oxide to 11-oxo-13R-manoyl, while RoFS1 and SfFS were able to produce 11-hydroxy manoyl oxide, in addition to 11-oxo-13R-manoyl oxide (Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: RoFS1 and SfFS produce 11-hydroxy manoyl oxide in addition to 11-oxo-13R-manoyl oxide from 13R-manoyl oxide.
source: while RoFS1 and SfFS were able to produce 11-hydroxy manoyl oxide, in addition to 11-oxo-13R-manoyl oxide (Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Two ACT candidates, CfACT1-6 and CfACT1-8, catalyze acetylation of deacetylforskolin.
source: Two ACT candidates, CfACT1-6 and CfACT1-8, were found to catalyze acetylation of 13b (Figure 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Expression of CfACT1-6 resulted in formation of a broad range of acetylated products of which forskolin constituted a minor fraction.
source: Expression of CfACT1-6 resulted in formation of a broad range of acetylated products of which forskolin constituted a minor fraction.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: CfACT1-8 exhibited high activity and specificity with efficient conversion of deacetylforskolin to forskolin and absence of detectable acetylated side products.
source: In contrast, CfACT1-8 exhibited high activity and specificity, with efficient conversion of 13b to forskolin and absence of detectable acetylated side products.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The entire and highly specific biosynthetic route to forskolin from GGPP has been established.
source: Identification of this enzyme establishes the entire and highly specific biosynthetic route to forskolin from its precursor, GGPP (Figure 9).
evidence: This claim is supported by the complete set of experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The highest forskolin producing yeast strain EVST21543 demonstrated genetic stability through several rounds of cultivation.
source: The highest forskolin producing strain, EVST21543, which demonstrated genetic stability through several rounds of cultivation, was grown in a 5 L fermenter using minimal medium under glucose-limited conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: Forskolin levels reached more than 40 mg/L of yeast culture in fermenter experiments.
source: Forskolin levels reached more than 40 mg/L of yeast culture.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from fermentation.

claim: Simultaneous accumulation of high titers of 13R-manoyl oxide and 9-hydroxy-13R-manoyl oxide at levels of 200 and 500 mg/L respectively indicated that the conversion of 13R-manoyl oxide to forskolin was far from complete.
source: Simultaneous accumulation of high titers of 13R-manoyl oxide (1) and 9-hydroxy-13R-manoyl oxide (3a) at levels of 200 and 500 mg/L, respectively, indicated that the conversion of 13R-manoyl oxide (1) to forskolin was far from complete.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and inference from the accumulation of intermediates.

claim: The intermediates 13R-manoyl oxide and 9-hydroxy-13R-manoyl oxide did not accumulate in the C. forskohlii root cork.
source: Interestingly, these intermediates did not accumulate in the C. forskohlii root cork.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observation.

claim: The identified CfCYP76AHs have discrete roles in forskolin biosynthesis.
source: The products profiles obtained with these enzymes revealed that the identified CfCYP76AHs have discrete roles in forskolin biosynthesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the experimental data showing different product profiles.

claim: Efficient monooxygenation at C-11 is catalyzed mainly by CfCYP76AH15 but also by CfCYP76AH8, CfCYP76AH17 and CfCYP76AH11.
source: Efficient monooxygenation at C-11 is catalyzed mainly by CfCYP76AH15 (but also by CfCYP76AH8, CfCYP76AH17 and CfCYP76AH11).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing enzyme activities.

claim: Monooxygenation at position C-9 is catalyzed exclusively by CfCYP76AH16.
source: Monooxygenation at position C-9 is catalyzed exclusively by CfCYP76AH16
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing enzyme specificity.

claim: Monooxygenation at C-1, C-6 and C-7 is catalyzed mainly by CfCYP76AH11.
source: monooxygenation at C-1, C-6 and C-7 mainly by CfCYP76AH11.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing enzyme activities.

claim: The set of identified CYP76AH enzymes could account for all the oxygenated positions in forskolin.
source: Collectively, this set of data displays the multifunctional roles of these enzymes. Together, they could account for all the oxygenated positions in forskolin.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the combined enzyme activities.

claim: Partial functional redundancy exists among the CYP76AH enzymes as demonstrated by varied oxygenation patterns observed in experiments with single enzymes.
source: Despite the complementary multifunctionality of the CYP76AH enzymes, partial functional redundancy is possible, as demonstrated by the varied oxygenation patterns observed in experiments with single enzymes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing overlapping activities.

claim: Certain C. forskohlii CYP76AH enzymes can accept oxygenated forms of 13R-manoyl oxide as substrates.
source: Moreover, certain C. forskohlii CYP76AH enzymes seem able to accept oxygenated forms of 1 as substrates which results in the observed shifts in profile toward higher decorated products when they are co-expressed in N. benthamiana (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from co-expression studies.

claim: The precise sequence of in planta 13R-manoyl oxide oxygenations cannot be deduced from the experimental results.
source: Although co-expression of CfCYP76AH11 and CfCYP76AH16 with either one of the three CfCYP76AH8, CfCYP76AH17 or CfCYP76AH15 in the engineered system resulted in biosynthesis of deacetylforskolin (13b) (Figure 5), the precise sequence of in planta 13R-manoyl oxide oxygenations cannot be deduced from the experimental results partly because all identified CfCYP76AHs accept 1 as substrate.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the experimental limitations.

claim: The co-expression of the CfCYP76AH encoding genes in the root cork of C. forskohlii and their partial functional redundancy or complementarity may constitute the basis for the chemical diversity of labdane terpenoids present in the root cork.
source: The co-expression of the CfCYP76AH encoding genes in the root cork of C. forskohlii and their partial functional redundancy or complementarity may in vivo constitute the basis for the chemical diversity of labdane terpenoids present in the root cork of C. forskohlii.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the observed enzyme activities and product diversity.

claim: In planta, the forskolin biosynthetic pathway appears to be entangled within a metabolic grid offering simultaneous production of a multitude of other diterpenoids.
source: In planta, the forskolin biosynthetic pathway would thus appear to be entangled within a metabolic grid offering simultaneous production of a multitude of other diterpenoids.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the observed enzyme promiscuity and product diversity.

claim: CfCYP76AH15 has very similar catalytic activities compared to rosemary CYP76AH4.
source: According to our results CfCYP76AH15 was found to have very similar catalytic activities compared to the rosemary CYP76AH4, an enzyme with a suggested role in the oxygenation of miltiradiene toward the synthesis of ferruginol (Zi and Peters, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing enzyme activities.

claim: CfCYP76AH15 and RoCYP76AH4 may represent orthologues.
source: Efficient formation of ferruginol as well as 11-oxo-13R-manoyl oxide, by both enzymes indicates that they may represent orthologues.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on similar enzyme activities.

claim: The ability of CYP76AHs to catalyze 11-oxo-13R-manoyl oxide formation has likely evolved convergently in different plants.
source: Thus, it is likely that the ability of CYP76AHs to catalyze 11-oxo-13R-manoyl oxide has evolved convergently in these plants (Figure 11).
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 11 and inference.

claim: The functional versatility of the CYP76 family may advance metabolic evolution by providing metabolic plasticity and flexibility affording synthesis of new diterpenoids.
source: These data highlight the functional versatility of the CYP76 family. The enzymes can exhibit broad substrate specificity which may advance metabolic evolution as they provide metabolic plasticity and flexibility affording synthesis of new diterpenoids.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the observed enzyme promiscuity.

claim: The promiscuity of CYP76AHs facilitates the expansion of the number of possible diterpenoids produced in nature and potentially serves to diversify and augment the phytochemical defense of plants.
source: This facilitates the expansion of the number of possible diterpenoids produced in nature and potentially serves to diversify and augment the phytochemical defense of plants.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the observed enzyme promiscuity and general knowledge about plant defense.

claim: The exclusive presence of the CYP76AH subfamily in Lamiaceae species may reflect gene duplications in a Lamiaceae ancestral species followed by expansion and neofunctionalization after speciation.
source: The exclusive presence of the CYP76AH subfamily in Lamiaceae species may reflect gene duplications in a Lamiaceae ancestral species followed by expansion and neofunctionalization after speciation (Figure 11).
evidence: This claim is speculative based on phylogenetic analysis and evolutionary inference.

claim: The only currently identified acyltransferases in diterpenoid biosynthesis are those involved in the biosynthesis of paclitaxel.
source: Interestingly, the only currently identified acyltransferases in diterpenoid biosynthesis are those involved in the biosynthesis of paclitaxel.
evidence: This claim is supported by knowledge of the field at the time of publication.

claim: Paclitaxel acetyltransferases show substantial regioselective promiscuity and belong to Clade V.
source: Those acetyltransferases show substantial regioselective promiscuity (Ondari and Walker, 2008; Walker and Croteau, 2000) and belong to Clade V (D'Auria, 2006; Tuominen et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The majority of ACTs identified in the root cork transcriptome of C. forskohlii, including ACT1-6 and ACT1-8, belong to Clade III.
source: whereas the majority of the ACTs identified in the root cork transcriptome of C. forskohlii, including ACT1-6 and ACT1-8, belong to Clade III (Figure 12).
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 12.

claim: Specific de novo production of forskolin at titers above 40 mg/L was achieved through a pathway consisting of 10 enzymatic steps catalyzed by eight heterologously co-expressed enzymes.
source: Specific de novo production of the highly functionalized diterpenoid at titers above 40 mg/L was achieved through a pathway consisting of a total of 10 enzymatic steps catalyzed by eight heterologously co-expressed enzymes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from yeast fermentation.

claim: The high forskolin titer achieved with no optimization steps highlights the potential to develop a microbial manufacturing platform for efficient and stereospecific production of forskolin.
source: This high forskolin titer, achieved with no optimization steps, highlights the potential to develop a microbial manufacturing platform for efficient and stereospecific production of forskolin with further fine-tuning of the biosynthetic pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the experimental results.

claim: There is a limitation in flux through one or several of the P450s involved in forskolin biosynthesis as evidenced by accumulation of intermediates.
source: Specifically for forskolin pathway, it seems clear that there is a limitation in flux through one or several of the P450s involved as we encounter accumulation of the intermediates, 300 mg/L and 500 mg/L of compounds 1 and 3a respectively, compared to forskolin (40 mg/L).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing intermediate accumulation and inference.

claim: Accumulation of only minute amounts of deacetylforskolin shows that CfACT1-8 is not a limiting step in the pathway.
source: Accumulation of only minute amounts of deacetylforskolin shows that CfACT1-8 is not a limiting step in the pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observation and inference.

claim: Accumulation of intermediates 13R-manoyl oxide and 9-hydroxy-13R-manoyl oxide was not observed in planta, likely signifying that the expression levels of the heterologous CYPs expressed in yeast are not properly balanced or their efficiency and activity can be affected negatively after incorporation into the yeast membrane.
source: Accumulation of 1 and 3a intermediates was not observed in planta (Figure 10—figure supplement 1). This likely signifies that the expression levels of the heterologous CYPs expressed in yeast are not properly balanced or their efficiency and activity can be affected negatively after incoorporation into the yeast membrane, while in the native plant host, the pathway exhibits optimized carbon flux and enzymatic efficiency.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of yeast and plant data and inference about the causes.

claim: P450s are notoriously difficult to express in high amounts in yeast and exhibit rather low Kcat values.
source: P450s are notorious difficult to express in high amounts in yeast and recognized as exhibiting rather low Kcat values (Jung et al., 2011; Renault et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research and general knowledge.

claim: Forskolin is the first example of a pharmaceutical diterpenoid produced entirely in yeast at titers relevant for industrial consideration.
source: Forskolin is the first example of a pharmaceutical diterpenoid produced entirely in yeast at titers relevant for industrial consideration.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental results and knowledge of the field.

claim: Mining for additional members of the CYP76AH family has the potential to facilitate the assembly of further optimized panels of mixed-species P450s for the biosynthesis of bioactive diterpenoids.
source: Our current study demonstrates that mining for additional members of the CYP76AH family has the potential to facilitate the assembly of further optimized panels of mixed-species P450s for the biosynthesis of bioactive diterpenoids.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the current study results.

claim: Combinatorial assembly including CYPs offers the opportunity to design production systems for diterpenoids that are currently inaccessible and to expand the chemical diversity of diterpenoids to production of compounds currently not known in nature.
source: This shows the great promise that combinatorial assembly including CYPs outside the CYP76AH subfamily may offer and the opportunity to design production systems for diterpenoids that are currently inaccessible due to their exclusive presence in rare or red-listed plants and to further expand the chemical diversity of diterpenoids to production of compounds currently not known in nature.
evidence: This claim is speculative about future applications based on the current study.
